title: Valcon's Appian and Mendix practices plus an explicit BPA unit make it a strong fit
content:
Valcon was upgraded on evidence rather than opinion. It holds two workflow platforms — Appian through First Technology, a partnership dating to 2015, and roughly ten years of Mendix work including 30-plus apps and Mendix on SAP — plus an explicit Business Process Automation practice. Its Appian delivery is in Dutch banking, insurance and transport. The assessment's conclusion is a strong fit.

The reason two workflow platforms read as a positive rather than as double slot occupancy is the seam involved. Process orchestration platforms decide when things happen and hold the running instance as mutable state; they are the class of tool the thesis attaches to, not the class it displaces. A firm with an explicit BPA practice has already sold clients on modelled processes, which is the conversation in which the missing append-only decision record becomes visible. The verticals reinforce it: banking, insurance and transport are where who approved this, under which rule is already a funded question.

One thing to resolve before acting: despite the strong-fit verdict, the row is still carried at priority 9, do not pitch. Nothing in the record explains that, and on the criteria the screen states, Valcon looks like it belongs in the pitch list. Treat the priority as stale until someone confirms it deliberately.
